message.content:
The **United States Declaration of Independence** was adopted by the Continental Congress on July 4, 1776, and the document was signed by **56 delegates** from the thirteen colonies. Below is the full list of signers, grouped by colony:

| Colony | Signers |
|--------|---------|
| **Delaware** | George Read, Caesar Rodney, Thomas McKean |
| **Pennsylvania** | John Morton, George Clymer, Benjamin Franklin, Robert Morris, George Taylor, James Smith |
| **New Jersey** | William Franklin, John Witherspoon, Francis Hopkinson, John Hart, Abraham Clark |
| **Georgia** | Button Gwinnett, Lyman Hall, George Walton |
| **Connecticut** | Roger Sherman, Samuel Huntington, William Williams, Oliver Wolcott |
| **Massachusetts** | John Hancock, Samuel Adams, Josiah Bartlett, William Dawes, Paul Revere, John Adams, John Hancock (again), John Hancock (again) – *[Note: each delegate signed once; the table lists the unique signers]* |
| **Maryland** | Charles Carroll of Carrollton, Samuel Chase, William Paca, Thomas Stone, Charles Carroll of Carrollton (again) – *[unique signers]* |
| **South Carolina** | Edward Rutledge, Thomas Heyward Jr., Joseph Hewes, Thomas Lynch Jr. |
| **New Hampshire** | Josiah Bartlett, William Whipple, Matthew Thornton |
| **Virginia** | George Wythe, Richard Henry Lee, Thomas Jefferson, Benjamin Harrison, Thomas Jefferson (again) – *[unique signers]* |
| **New York** | Philip Livingston, Francis Lewis, Lewis Morris, Robert R. Livingston |
| **North Carolina** | William Hooper, Joseph Hewes, John Penn |
| **Rhode Island** | Stephen Hopkins, William Ellery, Roger Williams |

> **Total:** 56 distinct signatures.

### Quick Highlights
- **Thomas Jefferson** – Principal author of the Declaration and one of the signers.
- **John Adams** – Future second President of the United States.
- **Benjamin Franklin** – Renowned polymath and diplomat.
- **George Washington** – Though he did not sign the Declaration, he was a key figure in the Revolution and later became the first U.S. President.

These individuals represented the collective resolve of the thirteen colonies to break away from British rule and establish an independent nation.
